metadata.title: PWP-001: Protein Extraction - Thermo Fisher Pierce RIPA / T-PER Lysis
metadata.purpose: Common protein extraction workflow compatible with BCA assay, SDS-PAGE, western blotting, ELISA, and downstream purification planning.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Confirm against the current manufacturer protocol, SDS, and local EHS rules before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Choose lysis reagent based on downstream use. RIPA is strong and useful for total protein/western; IP Lysis Buffer or M-PER is gentler for complexes or activity assays.
Keep all samples and buffers cold. Add inhibitors immediately before use.
Remove culture medium, serum, and debris by washing cells with cold PBS when compatible.
Plan aliquots to avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.

steps.action: Prepare cold lysis buffer with freshly added protease and phosphatase inhibitors.
steps.criticalNotes: Choose lysis reagent based on downstream use. RIPA is strong and useful for total protein/western; IP Lysis Buffer or M-PER is gentler for complexes or activity assays. Add inhibitors immediately before use.

steps.action: For adherent cells, place plate on ice, wash with cold PBS, remove PBS, and add enough lysis buffer to cover the monolayer.
Scrape cells thoroughly and transfer lysate to a pre-chilled microcentrifuge tube.

branches.condition: Use after s2 for adherent cells

steps.action: For cell pellets, resuspend pellet completely in cold lysis buffer and mix by pipetting or gentle vortexing.
For tissue, weigh tissue, add T-PER or selected lysis reagent at the validated weight-to-volume ratio, and homogenize on ice.
Incubate lysate on ice for 5-30 minutes depending on sample type and reagent.

parameters.rawText: Incubate lysate on ice for 5-30 minutes depending on sample type and reagent.

steps.action: Clarify lysate by centrifugation at high speed, cold temperature, for the selected reagent/sample workflow.

steps.action: Transfer the supernatant to a clean pre-chilled tube without disturbing the pellet.
Measure protein concentration using BCA or another compatible assay.

expectedOutputs: Record total protein concentration and total recovery per sample.
Check lysate quality by SDS-PAGE or western blot for target and loading-control proteins.
Avoid viscous DNA-rich lysates; shear or clarify if viscosity interferes with pipetting or assays.
Confirm lysis buffer compatibility with BCA/Bradford, IP, ELISA, or activity assay before committing samples.

troubleshooting.cause: Incomplete lysis, insufficient homogenization, poor sample storage.
troubleshooting.solution: Increase lysis time within compatibility, homogenize better, keep samples cold.
Clarify more thoroughly or shear gently if compatible.
Use fresh inhibitors and keep workflow cold.

troubleshooting.cause: Detergent, reducing agent, salt, or inhibitor incompatibility.
troubleshooting.solution: Choose compatible assay or dilute/dialyze/cleanup sample.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Treat biological lysates, animal tissue, antibodies, resins, imidazole, TMB, acids, reducing agents, and preservatives according to local EHS rules.
Keep proteins and antibody complexes cold unless the selected assay step specifically requires room temperature or incubation at a defined temperature.
Use protease and phosphatase inhibitors when preserving abundance or phosphorylation state matters.
Clarify lysates before assays or binding steps to reduce clogging, background, and nonspecific binding.
Record sample input, buffer composition, inhibitor lot, incubation time, spin speed, protein concentration, fractions, plate map, and downstream validation.
